items.title: Genie Search is now generally available
items.text: Genie Search is now generally available. Genie Search indexes your organization's knowledge in sources such as Google Drive, Jira, Confluence, and Workday, so Genie One can search all of that knowledge in one place. Azure Databricks indexes each document's permissions with its content and keeps both current, so users see only the documents that they can already access in the source. Genie Search also powers the following features in Genie One: Org directories: Find teammates, browse the org chart, and view profiles from Workday. See Browse org directories in Genie One. Search in Discover: Search Azure Databricks assets and content from connected sources in one place. See Use Genie Search in Genie One. Databricks recommends using Genie Search together with MCP connectors, which let Genie One access live data and take action in the applications your team uses.

items.title: Genie Ontology is now generally available
items.text: Genie Ontology is now generally available. Genie Ontology is the context layer that gives Genie One, Genie Code, and other AI agents a business-aware map of your organization. It combines modeled knowledge that you define in Unity Catalog semantics with learned knowledge that Genie extracts from your assets and usage.

items.title: Unifying SQL Pools: Upcoming changes to UI and APIs
items.text: Sections: What's changing and when; What this means for customers; Performance and cost considerations for new workspaces; What API consumers should update; Changes to GET API responses; Changes to PATCH API; Before unification (current behavior):; After unification (proposed behavior):; Next steps. SQL pools are Fabric Data Warehouse’s built-in workload management capability. They help administrators organize workloads and control how compute resources are allocated across them. SQL pool configurations are represented differently depending on whether a workspace uses the built-in or custom pool model. With unified SQL pools, we’re removing that distinction and representing all pools through a single configuration model across the UI and APIs. This removes the need to switch between built-in and custom modes, making SQL pool configurations easier to understand and manage consistently across the UI and APIs. This blog provides advance notice of upcoming changes to SQL pool configuration…

items.title: To support your FinOps practices, you can now opt in to compute cost attribution in BigQuery editions (Preview)
items.text: To support your FinOps practices, you can now opt in to compute cost attribution in BigQuery editions. This feature attributes billed compute charges directly to the query projects that use your administration project's reservation capacity. Allocating costs based on actual commitment and autoscaling slot usage lets you accurately track project-level costs and manage internal chargebacks. This feature is available in Preview.
